title: Brief Single-Session Body Neutrality Program for LGBTQ+ Adults in Central Alabama
official: Brief Single-Session Body Neutrality Program for LGBTQ+ Adults in Central Alabama
summary: LGBTQ+ individuals tend to have elevated risks for eating disorders (ED), possibly due to minority stress. For LGBTQ+ individuals living in rural Alabama, they tend to experience high levels of anti-LGBTQ+ structural stigma and limited access to LGBTQ+-specific resources, which engender compounded risk for ED development and reduced access to care. Brief digital single-session intervention that incorporates psychoeducation about minority stress and body neutrality may be efficacious in reducing ED risk and improve positive body image among LGBTQ+ adults in rural areas. Prior research from another lab developed a single-session intervention (Project Body Neutrality) among LGBTQ+ adolescents indicated immediate positive changes in body image constructs and psychological well-being. The present project evaluates and adapts Project Body Neutrality, specifically for LGBTQ+ adults in a rural high-stigma, low-resource region.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* At least 18 years old,
* Identify as LGBTQ+,
* Currently living in one of the following AL counties: Lee, Dallas, Lowndes, Autauga, Coosa, Elmore, Tallapoosa, Macon, or Russell
* Have internet access (either via computer/tablet, mobile phone, or community center \[e.g., library\])

Exclusion Criteria:

* Being less than 18 years old,
* Identifying as cisgender and heterosexual,
* Not living in central AL,
* Not having internet access.
